questions.question: Which statement best explains the relationship between perplexity and validation loss when evaluating language models?
questions.choice_A: Perplexity is the exponential of the average negative log-likelihood (cross-entropy) and decreases as validation loss decreases.
questions.choice_B: Perplexity is the derivative of validation loss with respect to the learning rate and increases as loss decreases.
questions.choice_C: Perplexity is a normalized accuracy metric and is unrelated to cross-entropy.
questions.choice_D: Perplexity measures semantic similarity and is computed from cosine distances in embedding space.

questions.question: In zero-shot evaluation of LLMs, which practice is most appropriate?
questions.choice_A: Fine-tune the model briefly on a subset of the test set to calibrate its outputs.
questions.choice_B: Provide only task instructions and possibly a format example without any labeled in-context examples.
questions.choice_C: Include several labeled examples in the prompt to teach the model the task.
questions.choice_D: Use reinforcement learning on the benchmark until performance plateaus.

questions.question: Which benchmark primarily tests coreference-based commonsense reasoning with fill-in-the-blank pronoun resolution?
questions.choice_A: PIQA
questions.choice_B: LAMBADA
questions.choice_C: Winogrande
questions.choice_D: OpenBookQA

questions.question: What is a key advantage of using an evaluation harness like EleutherAI's lm-evaluation-harness?
questions.choice_A: It automatically trains models to improve scores on benchmarks.
questions.choice_B: It replaces the need to set decoding parameters explicitly.
questions.choice_C: It converts generative tasks into supervised training objectives.
questions.choice_D: It standardizes prompts, tokenization, decoding, and scoring across many benchmarks, improving comparability.

questions.question: Why can lower perplexity fail to translate into higher accuracy on multiple-choice benchmarks?
questions.choice_A: Perplexity measures token-level predictive fit and may not reflect calibrated selection among discrete options.
questions.choice_B: Perplexity is only defined for character-level models.
questions.choice_C: Accuracy is invariant to tokenization while perplexity is not, making them mathematically identical.
questions.choice_D: Multiple-choice accuracy is computed from perplexity thresholds.

questions.question: Which description correctly characterizes HellaSwag?
questions.choice_A: A dataset focusing on arithmetic word problems requiring step-by-step calculation.
questions.choice_B: A commonsense inference benchmark where the model chooses the most plausible continuation among adversarially hard options.
questions.choice_C: A biomedical QA benchmark based on PubMed abstracts.
questions.choice_D: A code synthesis benchmark with unit tests for correctness.

questions.question: What is a common pitfall when reporting average scores across diverse benchmarks?
questions.choice_A: Averaging across tasks always favors smaller models.
questions.choice_B: Macro-averaging eliminates all variance, making significance testing unnecessary.
questions.choice_C: Unweighted averages can obscure domain-specific weaknesses and be biased if tasks vary greatly in difficulty and class balance.
questions.choice_D: Averaging is invalid because benchmarks use different licenses.

questions.question: Which practice best supports statistical significance when comparing two LLMs on a benchmark?
questions.choice_A: Compare single-run accuracies and declare significance if there is any difference.
questions.choice_B: Use a higher temperature to create more varied outputs and pick the best run.
questions.choice_C: Report micro-averaged precision only, since it is more stable.
questions.choice_D: Run multiple seeds, control decoding randomness, and apply paired tests or bootstrap confidence intervals on per-item outcomes.

questions.question: Which dataset is designed to test last-word prediction in broad-context narratives?
questions.choice_A: LAMBADA
questions.choice_B: BoolQ
questions.choice_C: ARC-Challenge
questions.choice_D: SciQ

questions.question: In few-shot evaluation, which aspect is most critical to report for reproducibility and fair comparison?
questions.choice_A: The number of training steps taken during evaluation.
questions.choice_B: The exact in-context examples, their order, and the prompt template used.
questions.choice_C: The model's total parameter count rounded to the nearest million.
questions.choice_D: The average GPU memory during inference.

questions.question: Which statement about ARC is accurate?
questions.choice_A: It evaluates only reading comprehension with yes/no answers.
questions.choice_B: It contains coding problems that require program synthesis.
questions.choice_C: It is a science question benchmark with an Easy and a Challenge set; the Challenge set is designed to resist simple heuristics.
questions.choice_D: It is a dataset of fill-in-the-blank narrative continuations.

questions.question: Why is controlling for data contamination crucial when evaluating LLMs on public benchmarks?
questions.choice_A: Contamination reduces inference speed on GPUs.
questions.choice_B: It ensures the model's validation loss remains constant across epochs.
questions.choice_C: Contaminated training data makes decoding unstable at low temperatures.
questions.choice_D: If benchmark items were seen during training, scores may reflect memorization rather than generalization, invalidating comparisons.

questions.question: Which metric is most appropriate to report for multiple-choice benchmarks like PIQA and HellaSwag?
questions.choice_A: Accuracy, possibly with normalized scores if the benchmark defines them.
questions.choice_B: BLEU score with n-gram smoothing.
questions.choice_C: ROUGE-L to capture long-span overlaps.
questions.choice_D: Perplexity per byte.

questions.question: What distinguishes BoolQ from many other QA benchmarks?
questions.choice_A: It uses open-ended generation with long-form answers only.
questions.choice_B: It consists of yes/no questions paired with passages, testing reading comprehension and verification.
questions.choice_C: It focuses on last-token prediction within literary narratives.
questions.choice_D: It requires multi-hop reasoning over tables and graphs.

questions.question: In reporting validation loss for LLMs, which detail most affects comparability across studies?
questions.choice_A: The color scheme used in training curves.
questions.choice_B: The batch size used for fine-tuning unrelated tasks.
questions.choice_C: The tokenization scheme and the log base used in cross-entropy (e.g., natural log vs. base-2) when converting to perplexity.
questions.choice_D: The order in which GPUs are listed in the appendix.

questions.question: Which statement best characterizes OpenBookQA?
questions.choice_A: A dataset requiring paraphrase detection between sentence pairs.
questions.choice_B: A code completion benchmark with strict unit tests.
questions.choice_C: A multiple-choice QA benchmark combining a small 'open book' of science facts with questions requiring reasoning beyond those facts.
questions.choice_D: A commonsense cloze benchmark focusing on pronoun resolution.

questions.question: Which methodological choice can inflate reported performance without reflecting true capability?
questions.choice_A: Fixing random seeds and decoding parameters across runs.
questions.choice_B: Selecting the best-performing prompt after testing many templates on the test set without a held-out validation set.
questions.choice_C: Reporting confidence intervals using bootstrap over items.
questions.choice_D: Disclosing model and evaluation code versions.

questions.question: Which description best fits PIQA?
questions.choice_A: A physics exam benchmark requiring numeric problem solving.
questions.choice_B: A dataset of physical commonsense questions where the model chooses the more plausible solution to a goal-oriented task.
questions.choice_C: A biomedical entity linking dataset.
questions.choice_D: A multilingual translation test suite.

questions.question: When averaging scores across tasks, what is a principled approach to avoid overemphasizing high-variance tasks?
questions.choice_A: Use unweighted macro averages exclusively.
questions.choice_B: Weight tasks or datasets by their reliability (e.g., inverse-variance weighting) and report both per-task and aggregate results.
questions.choice_C: Exclude any task where the model underperforms the mean.
questions.choice_D: Convert all metrics to perplexity before averaging.

questions.question: Which practice best improves reproducibility for LLM benchmark results?
questions.choice_A: Reporting only the final aggregated score to reduce clutter.
questions.choice_B: Publishing the exact prompts, decoding parameters (e.g., temperature, top-p), stop sequences, versions of the evaluation harness, and random seeds.
questions.choice_C: Relying on default settings because they are standardized across all toolkits.
questions.choice_D: Rounding per-task scores to the nearest 5% to minimize noise.
